firmwares.name: AISLING
firmwares.author: stephencummins
firmwares.about: Generative Irish ambient: harps in a jig's threes and a flute over a drone, with surf, wind and rain. Eight pieces that play forever.

firmwares.name: AMB-1
firmwares.author: charlesvestal
firmwares.about: Generative ambient after Eno's Music for Airports: breathing voices, bells on tape loops of unequal length, a gliding bass. Plays itself from switch-on.

firmwares.name: ATEK303
firmwares.author: animatek
firmwares.about: A TB-303-style acid bass line machine.

firmwares.name: Blop
firmwares.author: OSR-Experiment
firmwares.about: One-finger chord grids, chord rhythms, kick with sidechain, glide and reverb.

firmwares.name: Caravel
firmwares.author: BonszaiMusic
firmwares.about: Multi-engine synth firmware with DRONE, STASIS texture capture, Pair Morph, and per-track Random Morph and Morph Journey for evolving, ambient and experimental sound design. Sequencer, MIDI Learn, USB audio.

firmwares.name: Carnac OS
firmwares.author: OrbVorgis
firmwares.about: A dual-timbral wavetable synth after Carnac's standing stones: 15 morphing wavetable banks, seven voice architectures, a MAQ 16/3-style sequencer for modulated sequences and a chord sequencer for progressions, spring, tomb and tank reverbs. Its own installer also writes its wavetables. Built on X0X and Felucca.

firmwares.name: CHOPPAH
firmwares.author: profikid
firmwares.about: Breakbeat chopper: sixteen slices on the white keys, effect pads on the black, and a generator that rearranges the break as it plays.

firmwares.name: CS-1
firmwares.author: twochannels
firmwares.about: A Yamaha CS-80 in spirit: eight voices of two channels, high- and low-pass filters in series, ring modulator, the touch response and 22 tones from the owner's manual. A sound module played over MIDI.

firmwares.name: CTL-1
firmwares.author: charlesvestal
firmwares.about: A MIDI controller with its own sounds: velocity and aftertouch from the keys, scale chords on the black keys, an arpeggiator and Euclidean tracks.

firmwares.name: Daurade
firmwares.author: delirioux
firmwares.about: Generative French house after a certain robotic duo: a filtered loop opening over sixteen bars, a mix that pumps on every kick and a robot voice singing the hook. Ten styles, four knobs, drops, solos, the lead on the keys.

firmwares.name: DUB-1
firmwares.author: sbegueria
firmwares.about: Generative dub techno: chord stabs into a tape echo, FM pings on uneven loops, sub bass grooves. Plays itself; you steer it.

firmwares.name: DUELL
firmwares.author: OSCILL/R
firmwares.about: A multimorphing bitimbral synthesizer: two complete parts, three ways to play them together, and a morph that glides between two versions of every sound.

firmwares.name: Dungeon Tracker
firmwares.author: Bourbon Weather
firmwares.about: A four-track groovebox that is a dungeon crawler: your party plays the music, the rogue drums, the fighter bass, the cleric pads and the mage the melody. Step-program in a tracker or record live, and see how deep you get.

firmwares.name: ECHOFIELD
firmwares.author: Philip-Bos
firmwares.about: Granular sampler: a few seconds of sound become slow clouds, sparkles, tape loops and swells.

firmwares.name: Elixir
firmwares.author: dmajka
firmwares.about: Drum synth and sequencer, begun as a port of the Erica Synths LXR-02 firmware.

firmwares.name: Felucca
firmwares.author: hugelton
firmwares.about: The multi-engine, multitimbral synth and sequencer by Leo Kuroshita that SLOOP, Clipper and others grew from. In sabliran's web emulator.

firmwares.name: Flyfish
firmwares.author: delirioux
firmwares.about: One piece on the FM-1: Chopin's Étude Op. 10 No. 1 on a sampled Steinway D. It plays the étude, lets you shape it with rubato, touch and accents, practise it and move it. Built on Tuna and Felucca.

firmwares.name: FM-106
firmwares.author: PatttF
firmwares.about: The Juno-106 emulation of KR-106 ported to the FM-1: six voices on both cores, the BBD stereo chorus, 128 factory presets and a 1980s Roland look.

firmwares.name: FM-FAM
firmwares.author: davidamomusic
firmwares.about: DFAM-style 16-step sequencer and drum synth: two oscillators, parameter locks, random pages, scales.

firmwares.name: FoMni
firmwares.author: charlesvestal
firmwares.about: A chord harp inspired by the Omnichord: hold a chord, strum the keys.

firmwares.name: HYP-1
firmwares.author: RedtailWorks
firmwares.about: Hypnotic techno and acid: a breathing pad, a deep drone, a generative 303 line and grain over drums you sequence. Flip patterns on the bar, break it down, build it up. Forked from AMB-1.

firmwares.name: JAMTRACK
firmwares.author: Philip-Bos
firmwares.about: A backing band: drums, bass, chords and a synth line follow your chord progression in any key and time signature.

firmwares.name: JIANT FM
firmwares.author: juanjiant-bit
firmwares.about: A bio-synthetic groovebox: six tracks drawn as living beings, eight engines (FM6 with Dexed, analog, phase, voice), mutating macros and SLOOP's song mode. Still in development.

firmwares.name: KARMA
firmwares.author: Ariel Muchnik
firmwares.about: A four-track groovebox: an acid bass or a Juno-style poly, physical modelling, two dozen synthesis models and a drum synth. A 64-step sequencer with song mode, generators that write parts on one chord plan, pixel characters, and USB audio with six stems, MIDI out and DAW sync.

firmwares.name: Kris Jangle
firmwares.author: doohinkus
firmwares.about: A Christmas phrase game: it plays the start of a public-domain carol, you play it back on the keys.

firmwares.name: LOAF BREAKER
firmwares.author: FLEXOR-R
firmwares.about: FLEXOR's take on CHOPPAH: the Amen chopper with its own breaks and effects.

firmwares.name: LOOM-8
firmwares.author: charlesvestal
firmwares.about: Pocket groovebox: eight tracks on eleven engines (seven synths, a 303, sampler, break slicer, drum kit).

firmwares.name: Makohai
firmwares.author: delirioux
firmwares.about: A generative groovebox in the style of early-90s PC tracker music: six lanes (lead, arp, pad, bass, drums, sfx) composed live in ten S3M-scene styles. You mix styles instead of programming steps. Built on Tuna and Felucca.

firmwares.name: MAKU
firmwares.author: okumurari
firmwares.about: An ambience machine for DJ interludes: switch it on and a random world in key plays, four parts, buttons that are verbs, and the worlds you like breed new ones. Clock follow. Play it in the browser first.

firmwares.name: MANIFOLD
firmwares.author: stets43
firmwares.about: Generative just intonation: two layers of points wander a Tonnetz map, so every interval is pure. Nothing is sequenced.

firmwares.name: Melodee
firmwares.author: keremimo
firmwares.about: Total playing pleasure, far beyond Felucca: recording without quantize, microtonal scales, a Casio CZ-1, a bit-by-bit Dexed, scale modes made for an MPC Sample as its companion.

firmwares.name: Mighty Arp
firmwares.author: NickCulbertson
firmwares.about: A 4-op FM/subtractive synth built around a chance arpeggiator: hold a chord and chance plays the melody. 50 sounds plus RANDOM.

firmwares.name: MIN-1
firmwares.author: Reytian
firmwares.about: A tiny minimalist ensemble after Philip Glass: it starts playing when you switch on, you join whenever you like. In EASY mode every white key is a chord that fits. Four models, twenty pieces.

firmwares.name: NACHTFAHRT
firmwares.author: FartyPants
firmwares.about: Generative Berlin School: 1970s-style sequencer music that builds and drifts on its own.

firmwares.name: Niagara Drift
firmwares.author: evanyerburgh
firmwares.about: A drone synth: two drifting virtual-analog drones, each with its own part, swells, LFOs, effects and a sequencer.

firmwares.name: Ombak
firmwares.author: MadMooneyham
firmwares.about: Gamelan-inspired and meditative: you play the core melody, the ensemble weaves round it, every note shimmering with ombak beating.

firmwares.name: PaperLagoon
firmwares.author: hacha
firmwares.about: Generative environmental music: FM voices through tape echo and plate, wandering between seven worlds. Plays by itself.

firmwares.name: Penumbra
firmwares.author: Lunar Eclipse Forge
firmwares.about: A cinematic space drone you travel through, not one that plays itself. Five drone voices hold a pedal; turn PRESET and they glide to the next scene one voice at a time, or MORPH there by hand. Play VOX over it in key, loop it and the loop follows the key, or hold a key to bend and throw the sound.

firmwares.name: PERF-1
firmwares.author: deamonSLINKY
firmwares.about: Live performance: nineteen genres that play themselves while you steer, an auto-DJ, an acid line that answers itself, FM voices.

firmwares.name: Pocket GammaWave
firmwares.author: ShadowTune (GammaWave Audio)
firmwares.about: The companion to the GammaWave desktop synth: four industrial distortions, vowel and scream filters, an FFT spectrogram, a four-track tape deck screen and a song generator with 49 genres, trap and drill too.

firmwares.name: Polly
firmwares.author: charlesvestal
firmwares.about: A pocket arranger after the Yamaha QY70: eight-instrument styles on General MIDI sounds, steered by the chords you play.

firmwares.name: PULHRA
firmwares.author: 646timur-cell
firmwares.about: A minimal Elektron-style groovebox: four tracks, patterns in banks A to E, parameter locks, trig conditions, chains, an arpeggiator per track and per-pattern kits on the MONOFM sound core. A hard fork of Felucca.

firmwares.name: Rainbow Mode
firmwares.author: joshbartlettband-web
firmwares.about: A music toy for little hands (a Felucca fork).

firmwares.name: Sardine
firmwares.author: delirioux
firmwares.about: Live club mixing: four layers (lead, chord, bass, drums) always playing, with pattern modifiers that wait for the bar.

firmwares.name: SiDJ
firmwares.author: thomasj (tubesockor)
firmwares.about: Plays C64 SID music from HVSC on an emulated 6581 or 8580 and lets you remix every voice live: transpose, mute, solo, swap waveforms, bend envelopes and filter, add LFOs, ride the tempo. Out of the jack, as USB audio or over ASID to a real SID. MIDI clock from the tune, or the tune synced to yours.

firmwares.name: Sill
firmwares.author: delirioux
firmwares.about: Generative 90s eurodance, pickled in 1995: a song in intro, verse, pre-chorus, chorus and break, with lift, pump, vox and energy on the knobs, the hook, the groove and a key change up for the last chorus. Eight sets to store. On Felucca, after Tuna.

firmwares.name: Skiff
firmwares.author: illuminus5
firmwares.about: A six-track groovebox built on Felucca 1.1.5: fourteen synth and drum engines, a 64-step sequencer with chords, ratchets and locks, songs and a performance layer.

firmwares.name: Skiff Atlatl
firmwares.author: LIkst4
firmwares.about: A Skiff fork: analog, 303 and Plaits-style oscillators, a Minimoog voice, blendable filters and per-lane drum models.

firmwares.name: SLOOP
firmwares.author: isod89
firmwares.about: A live four-track groovebox: three synths and a drum machine, many synthesis engines and drum kits, a song mode played with your hands. SLOOP 2.3 in sabliran's web emulator.

firmwares.name: SPELLBOX
firmwares.author: pjac1810
firmwares.about: A talking spelling game after the 1978 Speak & Spell, with period LPC speech (in French).

firmwares.name: Tessera
firmwares.author: Theo Dainis (Rastapopolix)
firmwares.about: Generative music on four tracks: each plays its own steps, an arpeggio or one of 13 generators (Turing, Euclid, Markov, Constellation, Chord and more), and the tracks evolve, follow and modulate each other. EVOLVE and FORM grow phrases into songs; 16 mod cords connect anything. A Melodee fork.

firmwares.name: TRIBE
firmwares.author: apiel
firmwares.about: A ten-track groovebox built on X0X where any engine plays on any track: kicks, 909 and 808 voices, a 303, sixteen clips a track and scatter effects.

firmwares.name: Tuna
firmwares.author: delirioux
firmwares.about: Generative music built on Felucca: composer profiles write the music as it plays, you steer them. A work in progress.

firmwares.name: X0X
firmwares.author: charlesvestal
firmwares.about: A groovebox: 909, 808, two 303s and a break player. Pick a drum with a black key, set steps with the white keys, then PLAY.

firmwares.name: X0X-RMX
firmwares.author: Mr-Roboto (Oliver)
firmwares.about: X0X remixed after The Orb: banks and patterns reordered live per voice, Grids MAP and EUCLID drum generation, an extended TB-3PO with 22 scales and a morphing 303 waveform. Built on X0X.
